- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., high sentiment → high forecast → then sharp drop).
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is low or volatile; model fails to recognize mean reversion in low-sentiment periods.
- Forecast lags in early days of low sentiment; model delays correction, leading to persistent overestimation.
- High sentiment + recent high prices → model overreacts with upward bias; correct by reducing forecast slope.
- Low sentiment + recent high prices → model underreacts; correct by adding downward bias or smoothing.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; adjust downward by 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model fails to adjust quickly; apply a “sentiment decay” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days post-sentiment drop.
